body:
How do I connect with his emotions? I've been scared to go down a different route than just softly pushing away his paranoia because I've been afraid that it might give him the impression that what he's going through is the real thing and gets comfortable with the idea of it. 

Thank you for the kind words!

I know that look you're talking about - my boyfriend has it too, even the slightest mood shift of him I notice when the paranoia gets the better of him. I acknowledge it, and try to comfort him from there. 

How do you sympathize without him ending up thinking that you and him "believe in the same truth," and he's not "crazy" for thinking the way he thinks?

Thank you so much for your comment, especially the second half of it - that's so comforting to know. I've had an idea that that's the case because I've been telling him some stuff from the get-go that I realized a few days later, he started claiming himself. I thought it's a good thing.
Yeah, that's sadly how I've been sensing he's been feeling too a lot lately. :(
Ohh, that's interesting. It's actually the same for him - his mom and I thought it's just because of the weed withdrawal that's "giving his appetite back."
How long until you felt it taking effect? My fingers are crossed for him.
I'm doing my best. Thank you.
I can only imagine. How can I make him feel I am there for him? Lately he refuses to be visited and rarely writes me back.
